title: Images, layers and the registry
dek: An image is a Merkle tree of JSON documents and tarballs, each named by the sha256 of its exact bytes. This second part of a four-part Docker teardown pulls alpine:latest from Docker Hub request by request, takes its 9,218-byte index, its config and its one layer apart byte by byte, derives the three hashes of the same layer (digest, DiffID, ChainID), follows the layer into containerd's content store and overlay snapshots, compares Docker 29's two image stores, and pushes into a local registry to watch its storage, its Accept rules and its garbage collector.
byline: 23 October 2026 · Subject: moby@0367cbeb (Docker Engine 29.9.2) · Part 2 of 4 · Read from the source and the specs; measured where this machine allows
description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 taken apart, part 2: the OCI image as a tree of hashes, digest vs DiffID vs ChainID, tar layers and whiteouts, a measured Docker Hub pull, credentials, containerd's content store and snapshots, the two image stores, and a local registry's push path and GC.
og_description: Part 2 of a four-part Docker teardown at Engine 29.9.2 (0367cbeb): alpine:latest's 9,218-byte index and its 16 entries, three hashes of one layer reproduced from real bytes, whiteouts as tar entries and as kernel overlay objects, an anonymous Hub pull with hop timings, credential helpers, containerd's content store and snapshot GC labels, two meanings of "image ID", and a distribution v3.1.2 push and garbage-collection lab.
